findings.read_only_exception: The former selector allowed full-read/no-write/no-override requests onto a direct token. That constructor includes ambient Logon and Everyone among restricting SID alternatives. It cannot prove no writes where those identities have matching allow ACEs; a bounded Everyone-only audit also cannot establish a universal no-write/delete boundary. This is source-supported; no native read-only result has been claimed.
findings.native_capability_delete_failure: The exact native capability-only workspace token test denied two writes but permitted deletion of both outside targets. Removing identity SID alternatives alone has not established DELETE isolation under WRITE_RESTRICTED.
findings.native_acl_idempotence_failure: The repaired ACL blocks writes, but repeated repair returns (true,true,true), expected (false,true,false). Original logs contain no actual ACE layout. Mapped/split inheritance is a candidate requiring the newly added native trace.
findings.broker_scope: Public requests now require the existing broker. The broker still uses restricted tokens containing ambient identities and is not yet qualified by real broad-identity read-only/workspace boundary tests.
